solutions.17: a = 2, r = 4. 2 × 4ⁿ⁻¹ = 512, so 4ⁿ⁻¹ = 256 = 4⁴ and n = 5. It is the 5th term.
solutions.18: ar² = 12 and ar⁵ = 96. Dividing: r³ = 8, so r = 2 and a = 3.
solutions.20: Take a/r, a, ar. Product = a³ = 27, so a = 3. 3/r + 3 + 3r = 13 gives 3r² − 10r + 3 = 0, so r = 3 or 1/3. The numbers are 1, 3, 9.
solutions.22: b² = ac. LHS = (a² + ac)(ac + c²) = a(a + c) × c(a + c) = ac(a + c)². RHS = b²(a + c)² = ac(a + c)². Hence LHS = RHS.
solutions.24: (a) After 1 hour: 1,000. After 2 hours: 2,000. (b) 500 × 2ⁿ. (c) 500 × 2ⁿ = 64,000, so 2ⁿ = 128 and n = 7 hours.

solutions.20: In ΔADB and ΔBDC: ∠ADB = ∠BDC = 90°, and ∠ABD = 90° − ∠A = ∠BCD. So ΔADB ~ ΔBDC (AA). Hence AD/BD = BD/DC, so BD² = AD × DC.
solutions.21: The sun's rays make the same angle with the ground, and both objects are vertical, so the triangles are similar (AA). h/21 = 2/1.5, so h = 28 m.
solutions.22: ∠OAB = ∠OCD and ∠OBA = ∠ODC (alternate angles, AB ∥ DC). So ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (AA). AB/CD = 2, so the areas are in the ratio 4 : 1.
solutions.23: (a) ∠A is common, and ∠ADE = ∠ABC (corresponding angles, DE ∥ BC). So ΔADE ~ ΔABC (AA). (b) AD : AB = 2 : 5, so DE : BC = 2 : 5. (c) Areas: ΔADE : ΔABC = 4 : 25. So ΔADE : DBCE = 4 : (25 − 4) = 4 : 21.
solutions.24: (a) 1 cm = 25,000 cm = 0.25 km. Length = 1.5 km, breadth = 1 km. (b) Area = 1.5 × 1 = 1.5 km². (c) 1 cm² on the map = 0.25 × 0.25 = 0.0625 km². Map area = 0.5 ÷ 0.0625 = 8 cm².

notes.subtitle: General Term, Sum & Growth

concepts.title: Geometric progression
concepts.text: A list in which each term after the first is the previous term multiplied by a fixed number r (the common ratio).

concepts.title: General term
concepts.text: The nth term is tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹.

concepts.title: Sum of n terms
concepts.text: Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) when r > 1, and Sₙ = a(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r) when r < 1. If r = 1, Sₙ = na.

concepts.title: Geometric mean
concepts.text: The geometric mean of a and b (both positive) is √(ab).

method: Find a and r.
Use tₙ for a term and Sₙ for a sum.
Write powers of the same base to find n.
Check that the ratio is the same throughout.

example.question: Find the 7th term and the sum of 7 terms of 3, 6, 12, ….

practice.question: Find r for 81, 27, 9, ….
Find the 5th term of 2, −4, 8, ….
Find the GM of 3 and 27.
Which term of 1, 3, 9, … is 729?
Find the sum of 5 terms of 4, 12, 36, ….
The 2nd term of a GP is 6 and the 5th is 162. Find a and r.

tips: Check that the ratio, not the difference, is constant.
Use a/r, a, ar when the product of three terms is given.
Write the number as a power of r to find n.

notes.subtitle: Mirror Lines, Images & Invariant Points

concepts.title: Reflection
concepts.text: A reflection maps each point to its image on the other side of a mirror line, at the same distance from it.

concepts.title: Axes and origin
concepts.text: In the x-axis, (x, y) → (x, −y). In the y-axis, (x, y) → (−x, y). In the origin, (x, y) → (−x, −y).

concepts.title: Lines x = a and y = a
concepts.text: In x = a, (x, y) → (2a − x, y). In y = a, (x, y) → (x, 2a − y).

concepts.title: Invariant points
concepts.text: A point on the mirror line is its own image.

method: Identify the mirror line.
Change only the coordinate that the mirror line affects.
Plot the point and its image to check the distance.
For two reflections, apply them one after the other.

practice.question: Reflect (−4, 6) in the x-axis.

(a, b) reflected in the y-axis is (−4, 3). Find a, b.
Reflect A(1, 4) in the x-axis and then in the y-axis. Name the single transformation.

tips: Change only one coordinate for an axis reflection.
For a line x = a, the image is as far on the other side.
Label images with dashes: A′, A″.

notes.subtitle: Dividing a Segment & Centroid

concepts.title: Section formula
concepts.text: The point that divides the join of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) internally in m : n is ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)).

concepts.title: Mid-point
concepts.text: The mid-point is the special case m = n = 1.

concepts.title: Division by an axis
concepts.text: On the x-axis y = 0; on the y-axis x = 0. Take the ratio as k : 1 and solve.

concepts.title: Centroid
concepts.text: The centroid of a triangle is the mean of the three vertices.

method: Write the two end points and the ratio in order.
Put m with the second point and n with the first point.
For an unknown ratio, use k : 1.
Check the answer with the other coordinate.

Use k : 1 when the ratio is unknown.
Diagonals of a parallelogram have the same mid-point.

notes.subtitle: Slope, Intercept & Line Equations

concepts.title: Slope
concepts.text: The slope m = tan θ, where θ is the inclination. Through two points, m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁).

concepts.title: Forms of a line
concepts.text: Slope–intercept: y = mx + c. Point–slope: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

concepts.title: Parallel and perpendicular
concepts.text: Parallel lines have equal slopes. Perpendicular lines have m₁ × m₂ = −1.

concepts.title: Special lines
concepts.text: A line parallel to the x-axis has slope 0. A line parallel to the y-axis has an undefined slope (x = a).

method: Find the slope from two points or from the given line.
Change the slope for a perpendicular line.
Use the point–slope form with the given point.
Write the answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.

notes.subtitle: Similar Triangles, Areas, Maps & Models

concepts.title: Similar figures
concepts.text: Figures are similar when they have the same shape: equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides.

concepts.title: Tests for triangles
concepts.text: AA (two equal angles), SAS (one equal angle between proportional sides) and SSS (all sides proportional).

concepts.title: Areas
concepts.text: The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides.

concepts.title: Maps and models
concepts.text: For scale 1 : k, lengths are multiplied by k, areas by k² and volumes by k³.

formulas: Scale 1 : k: length × k, area × k², volume × k³
Right triangle with altitude BD: BD² = AD × DC
